Subject: Temporary reserve request + autoscale exception for Zephyr pilot (Sep 20 - Oct 4)

Team —

Quick ask to align on a short-term dedicated capacity carveout for Zephyr Health’s pilot. They want to run an accelerated evaluation of our LLM routing + caching features and are asking for a predictable slice so they can run consistent A/B tests. High level:

- Dates: 2026-09-20 00:00 UTC through 2026-10-04 23:59 UTC (two calendar weeks)
- Requested reservation: 120 GPU slots (p3-equivalent), split across 3 availability zones
- Expected workload: mixed long-context chat and batch reranks, median seq len ~1024, peak concurrency ~380 rps, steady-state ~180 rps
- Ask: temporary increase to min_capacity for the dedicated pool (autoscale policy exception) and a temporary carved burst lane for high-priority tests

I attached a short workbook with Zephyr’s traffic profile and our recommended buffer. They’re a strategic pilot — partner is committed to a co-marketing case study but we need to be sure this won’t destabilize other enterprise commitments.

Please advise: feasibility, recommended mitigations (quantized fallback / KV cache prefills), and whether we need an ops runbook + approval from finance for the cost delta. If feasible, I’ll request the formal reservation once we have sign-off and INFRA ticket.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: q4-zephyr-pilot-capacity-request.xlsx]

Subject: Re: Temporary reserve request + autoscale exception for Zephyr pilot (Sep 20 - Oct 4)

+1 on getting this scoped early. A few clarifying asks so I can sign off:

- Can you confirm model size(s) and whether they'll accept a 4-bit quantized variant as fallback? Quantized reduces memory footprint and helps with density.
- Confirm per-request average token generation expectation (tokens/resp) and if the rerank jobs are expected to run as large batches at specific windows.
- Do they require pinned GPU affinity (no preemption) or is preemptible ok with fast warmup?

Operationally I can make an exception to bump the pool min_capacity for the two-week window if we: 1) have a short ops runbook, 2) add a KV cache prefilling step before daytime tests, and 3) ledger the cost to the pilot budget.

If you can get me those details by EOD Thu 9/9 I’ll start a reservation request and draft the autoscale exception note.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Infrastructure Operations
[Attachment: capacity-runbook-draft-v1.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Temporary reserve request + autoscale exception for Zephyr pilot (Sep 20 - Oct 4)

Thanks — a couple technical notes from runtime:

- If Zephyr can accept a quantized variant for ~20% of requests we can squeeze more concurrency into the same slot count (approx +30% throughput for generation-heavy paths). We should make that an explicit fallback in the runbook.
- For long-context chat (1024) we need KV cache warmup. Recommend a prefilling window 10–15 minutes before their daytime tests.
- Rerank jobs: if they send large batch reranks (>= 1k items) please route those to a separate batch queue we can autoscale independently — avoids head-of-line blocking.

I’ll open INFRA-4827 to track the exemption and ops tasks. Necessities for me to approve: precise workload windows, which model variants to pin, and whether the partner accepts the quantized fallback during peak.

Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
